newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Colonial eyes 5 pct cut to bank cost ratio.
newsitem.headline: Colonial eyes 5 pct cut to bank cost ratio.

text.p: Australian-based insurance and banking group Colonial Ltd said on Monday it aimed to cut its cost to income ratio for its banking unit by five percent or more by late 1998 to early 1999.

"It is our intention that the bank reduce its cost/income ratio of around the mid-60s towards the end of 1997/98 to an early 60s, lates 50s target by the end of 1998 to early 1999," Colonial chief executive Peter Smedley told a luncheon.
Smedley told reporters after the luncheon they should look to the sensitivity analyses in the group's prospectus to find out how such cost-cuts would affect bottom-line profit.

"On page 71 of Colonial's prospectus a sensitivity analysis shows that a plus or minus five percent change in operating expenses for the group's banking operations would have a A$13 million impact on forecast profit after tax for the year ending December 31, 1997," Smedley said.
The prospectus forecasts a A$180 million after tax profit for the 1997 year.
Colonial plans to list on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges on May 12.
